title: Support Desk Standard for Fare Adjustments and Refunds, Wayfare Rides
content:
This standard governs money that rider support returns on charges of **Wayfare Rides (rider trips and fares)**: fare adjustments, which take back part of a charge, and refunds, which return a whole charge. A trip's net amount charged is everything charged to the rider on the trip less the fare adjustments and refunds booked on it.

## S1. One charge at a time

An adjustment or refund always names the single charge it returns money from; a request about a trip in general is resolved charge by charge.

## S2. Review window

An adjustment or refund may be made only within the review window. The review window is counted in calendar days from the charge date of the disputed charge: day 1 is the calendar day after the charge date, and the request must be made no later than the last day of the window. The length of the window is the ride option's review window in calendar days; the charge date is read from the charge record. Requests after the window are declined, whatever their merit.

| Charge date (hypothetical) | Window of 30 days: day 1 | Last day | Request on 10 July | Request on 11 July |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 June | 11 June | 10 July | within — may be handled | after the window — declined |

## S3. Adjustment reasons

- The clause *route inefficiency, only when the fare basis is recalculated and the rider did not change the route, takes back the fare charge amount minus the upfront fare less the member discount amount (the rider pays what was quoted)* is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis.
- The clause *fare above upfront, when the fare basis is upfront but the charge exceeds the upfront fare less the member discount amount, takes back the excess* is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis.
- **Wait time not incurred** takes back the part of a wait time charge above what the wait time rules allow.
- These three reasons are fare adjustment entries and leave the booking fee charged.

## S4. Whole-charge refunds

A whole charge is refunded for: duplicate charge, toll not incurred, airport surcharge not applicable, cancelled within grace, driver ETA exceeded, premature no-show, reserved driver late, and courtesy cancellation refund. The refund equals the charge less anything already returned on it.

## S5. Limits on what is returned

- The total returned on one charge — the fare adjustments and refunds booked against that charge — never exceeds that charge, and a charge already refunded in full is not refunded again.
- Support may return up to the ride option's support limit in total per trip, counting every fare adjustment and refund booked on the trip. A request that would take the trip above it, and any wrong drop-off location claim, is sent to the fare review team as a fare review for the disputed charge instead of being adjusted.

| Hypothetical support limit $15.00; already returned on the trip $9.00 | Result |
|---|---|
| New request of $6.00 (trip total $15.00) | within the limit — support may return it |
| New request of $7.00 (trip total $16.00) | above the limit — sent to the fare review team as a fare review |

## S6. Where the money goes

Refunds and adjustments go back to the original payment method; on a charge that is still outstanding they settle the outstanding amount first, under the rules for settling outstanding trip charges. Every rider amount computed under this standard is rounded half up to the cent once, at the end of its computation.

## S7. Dissatisfaction alone

A rider who did not like the route, the driver or the vehicle but whose charges follow these rules gets no adjustment.

superseded_clauses: fare_above_upfront, when fare_basis is upfront but the charge exceeds the upfront fare less member_discount_amount, takes back the excess

route_inefficiency, only when fare_basis is recalculated and rider_changed_route is false, takes back the fare charge amount minus the upfront fare less member_discount_amount (the rider pays what was quoted)
